scope: LOD1 and LOD3 only, rest / official kneeling rifle / zero-based official running raw frame 6. Front, quarter and rear views, 18 views total. Source and exports unchanged.
method: Exact final V/F, exact quantized weights applied to raw official deformation matrices. Exported corner normals transformed using same weights. One-sided EEVEE palette shading; reduced on-screen sizes, no near-LOD review or source edits. These are review sizes, not verified engine transition distances.
result: No gross clothing collapse, missing limb, exposed hand/finger/cuff hole, large outward spike, or obvious garment breakthrough found at the reviewed reduced screen sizes. Sleeve/hand shapes and main green silhouette remain continuous across all three poses.
observations: LOD1 keeps continuous shoulders and closed glove silhouettes in these views; the kneeling hand and wrist shapes remain recognizable at 400x520.
LOD3 shows expected coarse head/armor/finger silhouettes at 200x260. No conspicuous hand or cuff opening was visible.

LOD3 rear torso has pronounced dark angular shading below the white back plate, strongest in rest. A pure-emission, one-sided diagnostic removes the dark patch while retaining a filled green back silhouette: it is coarse surface/normal shading, not a large missing garment panel. Direct one-sided rear ray identification corroborates green coverage across the broad patch.
Running raw6 retains a narrow folded central tabard shape. This focused review found no gross rupture at the tested screen sizes; it does not supersede the nearest-LOD cloth contact audit.
limitations: These are selected static views, not a complete motion sweep of distance LODs.
Screen sizes are review targets, not verified in-engine LOD transition distances. Actual transitions depend on engine settings and projection.
Palette materials and exact exported normals were used for readable fit review; this is not validation of final texture baking or in-engine lighting.

Hidden internal overlaps, subpixel contacts, and microscopic cuff clearance were not exhaustively measured. The numerical open-edge check only covers the outer finger region; visible cuffs were reviewed in renders.
The coarsest torso shading can visibly pop when switching LODs and should be treated as a later visual LOD refinement, without claiming it is a geometry hole.
